lessons.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: Madrid’s scoring legacy
lessons.subtitle: A remarkable scoring rate and a European trophy haul

story.title: More than a goal per game
story.body: Cristiano Ronaldo played for Real Madrid from 2009 to 2018. The club’s official profile records 451 goals in 438 official matches, a scoring rate above one per game. Across competitions, 105 of those Madrid goals came in the Champions League.

story.title: A champion in Europe
story.body: His Madrid years also brought four Champions League titles. The profile presents those trophies alongside his club scoring records: 451 goals overall, including 105 in Europe’s leading club competition. His Madrid chapter combined individual output with repeated team success.

lessons.title: Fernando Arce: From Irapuato to Tijuana
lessons.subtitle: A long Mexican career brought him back to his hometown club

story.title: A first-division beginning
story.body: Fernando Arce took his early youth steps at América, then made his Mexican first-division debut with Irapuato on 28 October 2000. After three seasons, he moved to Veracruz in the Verano 2002 tournament, where he became a regular starter.

story.title: International and club milestones
story.body: Arce made his senior Mexico debut on 4 February 2003 and later played at the 2007 Gold Cup and Copa América. He joined Santos Laguna for Clausura 2008 and helped the club reach the final with a key semifinal goal against Monterrey. Later, his hometown team Club Tijuana signed him from Santos.

lessons.title: Duvier Riascos: Goals across continents
lessons.subtitle: A Colombian forward built a career in South America, China, and Mexico

story.title: A career starts in Colombia
story.body: Duvier Riascos began his professional career with América de Cali in 2005. His path later crossed into China, where he won the 2010 Chinese Super League scoring title while representing Shanghai Shenhua. The club’s signing profile celebrates the scoring crown as one of his standout individual achievements.

story.title: A chapter in Tijuana
story.body: After playing for Puebla in Apertura 2011, Riascos joined Club Tijuana for Clausura 2012. A 2019 Xolos retrospective recalls him as one of the club’s title-era figures and credits him with 23 goals in 65 matches for the team. It describes a career that continued after his Tijuana spell, including a move to Universidad Católica in 2019.
